text: Continuous Integration, or CI, is a common practice in modern software development. Every time a developer adds new code to a shared project, a CI system automatically starts an automated build. This means the code is compiled and checked without any manual work. The CI pipeline then runs a series of automated tests to make sure everything works correctly. By doing this regularly, teams can catch issues early, before they become serious problems. This saves time and reduces stress, because bugs are found quickly and fixed while they are still small. In short, CI pipelines help teams work faster and deliver better software.
